The Two Uber Technologies Stories Investors Were Weighing

The bullish narrative saw a path to market leadership, with a fair value near US$106, a price implied by assumptions such as 14.6% annual revenue growth and a 13.7% profit margin after three years.

The more cautious view anchored on a fair value of US$72.92, built on 13.1% topline growth but only 9.0% profitability and a risk that heavy autonomous investment and regulation could weigh on returns.

Uber Technologies pressed ahead with capital heavy robotaxis and delivery, committing about US$10b to autonomous vehicles and pursuing a US$14.8b Delivery Hero takeover backed by a BaFin approved offer document. That scale of spending challenged the bullish case for cleaner, high margin expansion when Q3 2026 results showed revenue at US$14,766m but net income at US$512m and net margin down to 3.5% from 49.2%. The evidence cut both ways.

The lesson is simple. When a story leans on margin expansion, do not stop at top line guidance. Track net income and the reported net margin against the original target, and check how much fresh capital is being committed to make that margin story work.
